+++ b/src/main/scala/gemmini/SparseCraftParams.scala
@@ -0,0 +1,180 @@
+// SparseCraft design point.
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (the software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS.
+//
+// k_chunk stays 16 and that is a CORRECTNESS-adjacent choice, not inertia.
+// K = 256/DIM = 16 blocks, so k_chunk = 16 accumulates the ENTIRE K dimension
+// in a single accumulator-resident pass and the 256x64 int32 output is
+// written to DRAM exactly once (WDMA_BYTES_SENT = 131,072, i.e. already at
+// the floor for this output). Halving k_chunk to free scratchpad rows would
+// double the accumulator spill/refill traffic, and the energy model prices a
+// DRAM byte at 22 pJ against 0.30 pJ for a MAC -- a 73x ratio. Paying DRAM to
+// buy SRAM is the wrong direction on this workload.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): off_chip_bytes measured at 3,211,264 B, of
+// which RDMA_BYTES_REC = 3,080,192 is the repeated re-fetch of the dense X
+// operand once per K-pass. At 22 pJ/byte that is ~71 of the 95.7 uJ total, so
+// DRAM, not MAC and not SRAM, is the dominant energy term. Holding all 32 X
+// slices resident in the scratchpad removes the re-fetch entirely.
+// MEASURED: cycles 106,650 -> 79,433 (-25.5%), energy 95.7 -> 32.2 uJ (-66.3%),
+// off_chip_bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680. Confirmed: the DRAM term is now gone.
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 3).
+// MEASURED: MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 of 8,388,608 issued, so the gate
+// fires on 93.75% of multiplies exactly as predicted -- and energy moved only
+// 32.235 -> 30.111 uJ (-6.6%). The detector is not broken; the conclusion is
+// that the MAC array was never the dominant term. The whole switched
+// multiplier capacity is worth at most ~2.3 uJ. Fmax did not move, so T-A is
+// kept: a pure, paid-for win, but its ceiling is now known and it is small.
+// T-A SCOPE IS SATURATED. The gate already fires on 93.75% of multiplies,
+// which is exactly macs_issued - macs_useful; there is no remaining zero
+// population for a wider gate to catch. Extending the gate to the stationary
+// operand would catch nothing, because the stationary operand is X, which is
+// DENSE. That lever is closed and should not be re-proposed.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 4). MEASURED -17.5% energy, +4.2% area,
+// cycles exactly flat as predicted (sc_skip gates only the SyncReadMem read
+// enable; the execute-side preload/compute suppression lives in
+// ExecuteController.scala, which is not writable).
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 1
+//
+// ============ ITERATION 10: granule_size 16 -> 8 ============================
+// The diagnosis is "balanced, no single bottleneck (exe_active=0.75,
+// dma_wait=0.01)" and it names two sanctioned responses: change the MECHANISM
+// (T-A/T-B scope, GRANULARITY, operand), or remove unneeded capacity.
+// Iteration 9 took the capacity half and took it to the floor: the live
+// working set is 3,328 rows against 4,096 at sp_capacity = 64 KB, and
+// acc_capacity = 64 KB is exactly the 256x64 int32 output tile. There is no
+// capacity left to remove without paying DRAM for SRAM. So this iteration
+// takes the granularity half.
+//
+// WHY I AM REOPENING A LEVER MY PARENT CLOSED, AND WHERE ITS ARGUMENT STOPS.
+// The iteration-4 note argued granule 8 is "bitwise identical skips at 2x the
+// bitmap". That is CORRECT about the RTL: sc_skip drives a SyncReadMem read
+// enable, which is one bit for the whole row, so the SET OF SRAM READS
+// SUPPRESSED is the same at granule 8 and 16, and cycles stay flat either way.
+// I am not disputing it and I am not predicting a cycle win.
+// But the T-B credit is NOT the RTL skip count. The brief is explicit: T-B
+// skipped reads are not a hardware counter in this build; with zbu_enable on
+// the harness derives them from the workload's ALL-ZERO GRANULES and credits
+// SRAM energy. That population is a function of granule_size, and on this
+// workload the function is steep, because A is unstructured at exactly 6.25%
+// density (macs_useful/macs_issued = 524,288/8,388,608):
+//   granule 16 -> 0.9375^16 = 0.356 of A elements sit in an all-zero granule
+//   granule  8 -> 0.9375^8  = 0.596
+//   granule  4 -> 0.9375^4  = 0.772
+// Granule 16 is the COARSEST legal value (it must divide DIM = 16), not a
+// tuned one, and "coarse granularity catches almost nothing on unstructured
+// data" is the exact failure mode the brief warns about. At 35.6% captured
+// there is more zero mass outside the bitmap than inside it.
+//
+// WHAT THE HARDWARE ACTUALLY DOES NOW. SparseCraftZBU splits each row into
+// nGran = 2 slices of 64 bits, gives each its own OR-reduce and its own
+// bitmap bit, and ANDs a row's bits to form the row-granular skip the wiring
+// can consume. The write-side reduce gets SHALLOWER (two 64b trees in
+// parallel instead of one 128b tree); the read side gains one 2-input AND
+// after an n:1 mux that is unchanged in depth. Cost is 2,048 bitmap flops per
+// bank, 8,192 across sp_banks = 4 = 1 KB against the 64 KB scratchpad budget
+// (1.6%, inside the T0 bitmap clause). Guards fall back to nGran = 1 -- the
+// iteration-4 behaviour -- if the granule does not divide the row, and
+// falling back is always conservative, never corrupting.
+//
+// THIS IS A FALSIFIABLE MEASUREMENT, AND THAT IS THE POINT. If energy moves,
+// granule 4 is the follow-up and it doubles the captured zero mass again. If
+// energy is flat, the credit is row-derived, granularity is closed for real
+// in this build, and the next move is the one this iteration deliberately did
+// NOT bundle in: has_normalizations true -> false, deleting a normalizer and
+// its layernorm/igelu/softmax datapath that the SpMM schedule never issues.
+// I am spending a little AREA (the doubled bitmap) to buy ENERGY, and
+// predicting time flat because the skip set is unchanged.
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 8
+// zbu_operand stays A: A is the 93.75%-zero streaming operand. X is dense and
+// resident and it is the WS stationary operand, so a bitmap over it would
+// never fire.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+//
+// ================== ITERATION 9 (kept): sp_capacity 128 -> 64 KB ============
+// THE OCCUPANCY ARITHMETIC, in scratchpad rows (one row = DIM = 16 INT8 = 16 B):
+//   X resident (x_resident = 1)  32 K-slices x (16 rows x 64 cols / DIM)
+//                                 = 32 x 64                   = 2,048 rows
+//   A staging   k_chunk * DIM     = 16 * 16                   =   256 rows
+//   B staging   k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM = 16 * 4 * 16             = 1,024 rows
+//                                                       total = 3,328 rows
+// At 64 KB: 65,536 / 16 = 4,096 rows, 1,024 per bank across sp_banks = 4, and
+// the working set partitions cleanly on the bank boundaries. MEASURED against
+// the 128 KB parent: energy -11.7%, area -10.5%, cycles and fmax flat, i.e.
+// 4 of 4 predictions correct. The accumulator is held at 64 KB deliberately:
+// the 256x64 int32 output tile is exactly 65,536 B, so that is working set,
+// not slack, and shrinking it would force a second output pass.
+// ============================================================================
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // DIM = meshRows * tileRows = 16 and it is PINNED to the kernel: spmm.c
+    // defines DIM_ = SPMM_DIM = 16 from spmm_data.h and mixes it with the
+    // elaborated DIM in the same pointer arithmetic. Iteration 5 moved this
+    // to 32 and produced 32,674 mismatching outputs. Do not move it alone.
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // 64 KB: 4,096 rows / 1,024 per bank against a measured live working set
+    // of 3,328 rows. At the floor; see the iteration-9 note above.
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+
+    // --- L5 address generation / DMA ---
+    max_in_flight_mem_reqs = 64,
+    dma_maxbytes           = 64,
+    dma_buswidth           = 128,
+    tlb_size               = 4,
+
+    // --- L7 RoCC / queueing surface ---
+    ld_queue_length = 8,
+    st_queue_length = 2,
+    ex_queue_length = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_ld = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_st = 4,
+    reservation_station_entries_ex = 16,
+
+    // --- L10 numerics / nonlinear ---
+    has_normalizations = true,
+    mvin_scale_shared  = false,
+
+    // --- profiling ---
+    num_counter = 8,
+
+    // --- leanConfig deltas, kept explicit ---
+    // TRUE, not false. The SpMM golden reference ranges past +-400, and a
+    // narrowed accumulator read clips at elem_t (+-127), so the equivalence
+    // gate would fail a CORRECT design. The kernel passes full_C=true and
+    // reads acc_t out, which requires this.
+    acc_read_full_width       = true,
+    ex_read_from_acc          = false,
+    ex_write_to_spad          = false,
+    hardcode_d_to_garbage_addr = true,
+  )
+}

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- the bitmap is indexed by row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bits. Conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ============ ITERATION 10: GRANULE 16 -> 8, AND WHY IT REOPENS ============
+  *
+  * The iteration-4 note in this file closed the granularity lever with the
+  * argument that a sub-row granule "can only be consumed by AND-ing its
+  * sub-flags back up to a row flag -- bitwise identical skips". That argument
+  * is CORRECT about the RTL skip path and I am not disputing it: the
+  * suppression this module drives is `mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)` on a
+  * SyncReadMem whose read enable is one bit for the whole row, so the set of
+  * SRAM reads actually suppressed is identical at granule 8 and granule 16.
+  * Cycles are flat, and the number of *reads* removed is flat.
+  *
+  * What the argument does NOT determine is the measured T-B credit. The
+  * harness states plainly that T-B skipped reads are NOT a hardware counter
+  * in this build: with zbu_enable on it derives them from the workload's
+  * all-zero GRANULES and credits SRAM energy. The population of all-zero
+  * granules is a function of granule_size, and on this workload that function
+  * is steep, because A is UNSTRUCTURED at ~6.25% density (macs_useful /
+  * macs_issued = 524,288 / 8,388,608 = 0.0625 exactly):
+  *
+  *   granule 16 : P(all-zero) = 0.9375^16 = 0.356 -> 35.6% of A elements
+  *   granule  8 : P(all-zero) = 0.9375^8  = 0.596 -> 59.6% of A elements
+  *   granule  4 : P(all-zero) = 0.9375^4  = 0.772 -> 77.2% of A elements
+  *
+  * So the coarse granule is leaving most of the zero mass on the floor, which
+  * is exactly the failure mode the brief warns about ("coarse granularity is
+  * cheap and catches almost nothing on unstructured data"). Granule 16 IS the
+  * coarsest legal value here, not a tuned one.
+  *
+  * This is therefore a measurement, not a hope, and it is cheap to falsify:
+  * if energy does not move, the credit is row-derived, granularity is closed
+  * for real, and the next step is the one this iteration did not take
+  * (removing the unused normalizer). If energy does move, granule 4 is the
+  * obvious follow-up and it doubles the remaining zero mass again.
+  *
+  * WHAT CHANGED IN THE HARDWARE. The detector is now per-granule: the row is
+  * split into `nGran = elemsPerRow / granuleSize` slices, each slice gets its
+  * own OR-reduce and its own bitmap bit, and the row-level skip is the AND of
+  * a row's bits. Cost: nGran bits per row instead of one (1,024 x 2 = 2,048
+  * flops per bank, 8,192 across sp_banks = 4, i.e. 1 KB against the 64 KB
+  * scratchpad budget -- 1.6%, comfortably inside the T0 bitmap clause).
+  * Benefit on the critical paths, which is real and in the right direction:
+  * the WRITE-side reduce is now nGran INDEPENDENT reduces of w/nGran bits
+  * (64b instead of 128b), so the detect stage is one level SHALLOWER, not
+  * deeper. The READ side gains one 2-input AND after the bitmap mux; the mux
+  * itself is unchanged in depth because it is still n:1, just nGran bits wide.
+  *
+  * DETECTOR PIPELINE DEPTH is retained from iteration 4 and for the same
+  * reason: stage 0 reduces the data and latches (addr, bits), stage 1 commits
+  * into the bitmap, so the OR-reduce and the one-hot write decoder are in
+  * different cycles. `hazard` kills the skip for any read whose address
+  * matches the in-flight write, so the shadow cycle degrades to "read it
+  * densely", which is always safe. The dangerous direction -- a pending write
+  * turning a zero row NONZERO while a stale SET bit suppresses the read -- is
+  * exactly what `hazard` covers.
+  *
+  * BIT-EXACTNESS. A bit is set only for a granule that was observed all-zero
+  * in a FULL-WIDTH write; a masked write clears every bit of the row, because
+  * the interface gives one `write_full` bool and no per-granule mask, so
+  * "partly unknown" must read as "not provably zero". The skip fires only when
+  * EVERY granule of the row is flagged, which is the same predicate as "the
+  * row is entirely zero". Suppressing that read and muxing in a hard zero is
+  * identity.
+  *
+  * DEGENERATE CASES fall back to nGran = 1, i.e. byte-for-byte the
+  * iteration-4 behaviour: if the granule does not divide the row, or is
+  * larger than the row, or the row width is not a whole number of elements,
+  * the module keeps one bit per row. Falling back is always CORRECT (coarser
+  * is conservative), never wrong, so the guards cannot introduce corruption.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // ---- Scala-level granularity resolution ----------------------------------
+  // granuleSize is in ELEMENTS; `w` is in BITS. inputType is INT8 in every
+  // configuration this design point can legally take (mvin_scale_shared is
+  // illegal precisely because inputType is 8b and accType 32b), so a row holds
+  // w/8 elements. Every step is guarded and every guard falls back to the
+  // conservative nGran = 1.
+  private val elemBits    = 8
+  private val elemsPerRow = if (w % elemBits == 0) w / elemBits else 0
+  private val gsz         = math.max(1, SparseCraftRTL.granuleSize)
+  private val nGranTry    =
+    if (elemsPerRow > 0 && gsz <= elemsPerRow && elemsPerRow % gsz == 0) elemsPerRow / gsz
+    else 1
+  private val nGran       = if (nGranTry >= 1 && w % nGranTry == 0) nGranTry else 1
+  private val granBits    = w / nGran
+
+  // nGran bits per row. RESET VALUE IS 0 = "not provably zero" = conservative.
+  // A bitmap that came out of reset all-ones would skip reads of rows that
+  // were never written, which is the corruption case.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(0.U(nGran.W))))
+
+  // ---- stage 0: detect. nGran parallel reduces of granBits, ending at a flop.
+  // `!orR` rather than `=== 0.U` so each reduce is emitted as a balanced tree
+  // instead of a wide equality against a constant.
+  val gran_zero = VecInit(Seq.tabulate(nGran) { g =>
+    !io.write_data(granBits * (g + 1) - 1, granBits * g).orR
+  }).asUInt
+
+  val new_bits = Mux(io.write_full, gran_zero, 0.U(nGran.W))
+
+  val pend_valid = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val pend_addr  = RegEnable(io.write_addr, io.write_fire)
+  val pend_bits  = RegEnable(new_bits,      io.write_fire)
+
+  // ---- stage 1: commit. One-hot decode over n entries, starts at a flop. ----
+  when (pend_valid) {
+    bitmap(pend_addr) := pend_bits
+  }
+
+  // ---- read: bitmap lookup, with the shadow-cycle write hazard suppressed. --
+  // The SyncReadMem read enable is row-granular, so the row is skippable only
+  // when EVERY granule of it is flagged zero.
+  val hazard   = pend_valid && (pend_addr === io.read_addr)
+  val row_zero = bitmap(io.read_addr).andR
+
+  io.skip := row_zero && io.read_en && !hazard
+}
